insights.summary: At Choice International's INSIGHTX 2026 meet (note posted 23 Jun 2026), Prizor guided FY27 revenue growth of about 50-60% and repeated its target of 1 crore cameras a year by FY30-31. It sold about 8 lakh cameras in FY26, which meets the 7-8 lakh figure from March, and ran camera assembly at about 50% of its 16 lakh capacity. Management says raw material is secured for the next year and the higher year-end inventory was deliberate, built ahead of a chip and memory shortage.

what_changed.text: First revenue guidance: FY27 growth of ~50-60% (on FY26's ₹153 Cr, about ₹230-245 Cr)
FY26 volumes of ~8 lakh cameras reported, meeting the 7-8 lakh guided in March
Inventory build at FY26-end explained as deliberate stocking ahead of a component shortage

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: Post-STQC, an INR 100 Bn domestic market has effectively re-opened as Chinese brands (historically ~70% share) vacate

analyst_questions.answer: Only 1-2 months of supply affected, covered by buying ahead; supply locked through next year, SoC chips from Taiwan.
The inventory build is deliberate, ahead of a possibly worse supply situation, so working capital was higher at FY26-end.
CCTV EBITDA margin is about 4-5 points above displays, which are made by third parties; price increases are passed to distributors with about a 1-month lag.

red_flags.text: Higher working capital at FY26-end is explained as deliberate stocking; check that inventory and receivables come down as the shortage eases.
STQC rules so far cover only IP cameras; DVR/analog (half the market) is still under review, and IP is only ~35% of Prizor's camera sales.
Second-hand source: a broker's summary of a management meet, posted on X.

watch_next: H1 FY27 revenue growth against the 50-60% FY27 guide

business_snapshot.what_they_make: CCTV cameras (~77% of revenue; IP cameras ~35% of that) and displays made by third parties (~23%)
business_snapshot.customers: Pure B2B through distributors and dealers; government orders through GeM
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: STQC rules pushing out Chinese brands from a ₹10,000 Cr market (Prizor share 1.5%), a ~6-year replacement cycle, price increases
